Cancelling an order now sends the customer one e-mail through the existing `Notifier` → `MailTransport` path, to their registered address, with the order id in the subject. `run_tests` passes.

- **`OrderService.cancel`** publishes a new `OrderCancelled(orderId, customerId)` event (in `orders/api`). Cancelling an order that is already cancelled does nothing, so a repeat cancel cannot send a second mail.
- **`OrderCancellationNotifications`** (new, in `notifications/internal`) listens for that event after the cancellation commits. It looks up the address with `CustomerFacade.emailOf` and sends subject `Order <id> cancelled`.
- **`OrderCancellationMailTest`** (new) checks that cancelling once sends exactly one mail to the right address with the id in the subject, that a second cancel adds nothing, and that a placed-but-not-cancelled order sends nothing.

If a customer has no registered address, no mail is sent and nothing is logged. Say if you would rather that case fail loudly.
